title: Console MiniWaypoints: compact cost & trace cards scope rebaseline
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Background: The Console Insights team must deliver a minimal, deployable surface that surfaces per-route cost and a simple trace latency signal for the alpha release. The original PRD included expanded drilldowns, long-tail trace visualizations, and a full cost breakdown table. Given timeline and cost constraints, we are rebaselining to a compact card approach (MiniWaypoints) that provides targeted signals without full exploratory tooling. This ticket captures the revised scope, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and implementation notes for the reduced surface.
acceptance_criteria: MiniWaypoints implemented as two card types on the Routes overview: (1) Cost Snapshot (per-route 24h cost estimate + 7d trend sparkline) and (2) Trace Health (p50/p95 latency & error-rate indicator).
Cards load within 400ms on cached route pages under standard staging traffic profile (measured via synthetic).
Backend provides aggregated cost and latency endpoints that return data in <250ms P95 for cached responses and <500ms for cold responses.
UX includes hover tooltips explaining metric definitions and a link to ‘View full telemetry’ that routes to advanced views (out of scope for this slice).
Feature gated behind 'miniwaypoints' config flag; rollout supports off-by-default, 10% canary, then 100% after smoke checks.
Automated e2e tests cover card rendering and primary metric values using mocked telemetry fixtures; performance test added to CI job 'console-telemetry-smoke'.
updates: 2025-03-01 - Aisha Kaur: Ticket created after PM sync; original PRD trimmed to focus on high-value signals. Linked to parent scope PM-32019.
2025-03-03 - Liam Chen: Eng review: can implement aggregated endpoints with a new summarization lambda; asked for tighter SLAs on response time. Marked dependency ENG-17422 for endpoint work.
2025-03-05 - Design review (Maya Ortiz): Provided two compact card mocks and accessibility checklist. Requested clearer tooltip copy and 48px minimum tap target for mobile.
2025-03-07 - PM decision: Remove full cost breakdown table from alpha; replace with 7-day sparkline + percentile compare badge. This avoids additional DB joins and shipment risk.
2025-03-09 - QA plan drafted by S. Patel: e2e test matrix and performance smoke added; ask eng to expose feature flag endpoint for canary.
2025-03-10 - Liam Chen: Implementation plan posted; backend prototype in-progress, UI skeleton merged behind feature flag (WIP).
decision_rationale: Time-to-value: compact cards deliver the highest signal per engineering hour and address immediate customer ask for cost visibility.
Cost & risk: removing full table and deep trace explorer avoids heavy aggregation work and large data export which were gating delivery.
Observability ROI: p95 latency + error badge surfaces reliability problems fast; teams can still navigate to full telemetry later.
Rollout safety: feature-flagged incremental rollout minimizes blast radius and gives stakeholders a clear rollback path.
qa_plan: QA will validate functional rendering, metric accuracy against synthetic fixtures, accessibility (contrast and keyboard focus), and performance (card load P95 < 400ms). A post-release verification checklist will be used during canary window.
rollout_plan: Ship behind `miniwaypoints` feature flag (default off in prod).
Canary: enable for 10% of orgs for 48 hours; run smoke and telemetry checks (error spikes, latency regressions).
If canary stable, increase to 50% for 24 hours, then 100% after sign-off from SRE and product.
Provide rollback playbook: disable feature flag + invalidate route cache; expected rollback time < 30 minutes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggregation endpoints may introduce added DB load. Mitigation: cache computed values in Redis and pre-aggregate hourly buckets; limit query cardinality to top N routes.
Risk: UX could be misinterpreted without drilldowns. Mitigation: add explicit tooltip copy and a ‘why this matters’ help modal linking to docs.
Risk: Performance regressions during peak traffic. Mitigation: feature flag can be disabled immediately; monitor trace and error dashboards closely during rollout.
